title: Prevalence of Co-payment Activities in Schools
what_it_is: Prevalence of Co-payment Activities in Schools

sections.label: School activity co-payment monitoring
sections.summary: MOE does not monitor co-payment activities but reminds schools payments should be affordable, with Edusave and MOE funds available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) whether the Ministry monitors the number of student activities in schools that involve co-payment by students; and (b) of such activities, what proportion is (i) compulsory, (ii) on an opt-out basis and (iii) on an opt-in basis but with 50% or more of eligible students participating.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: We do not actively monitor whether such activities involve co-payment from students, nor do we stop schools from making collections for these activities, as we believe that families should play a part in supporting their children in education as part of their familial responsibility.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: However, we regularly remind schools that such payments should not be excessive and should be affordable to parents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: Students can also opt to pay for these activities using their Edusave accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: For students from less advantaged backgrounds, schools can further subsidise or even fully pay the cost of their participation using specific funds provided by the Ministry of Education (MOE), such as the School-based Financial Assistance Grant and the Opportunity Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: Most importantly, no Singaporean student will be deprived of an educational opportunity because of his or her family's financial circumstances.

sections.label: Opportunity Fund usage update
sections.summary: In the last two years, 60% of Opportunity Funds paid for students' additional learning opportunities, ensuring no student is denied quality education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Just to give an update, in the last two years, 60% of the Opportunity Funds are used to pay for students' additional learning opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: So, I really want to assure the Member and the House that no Singaporean student will be denied access to quality education because of their families' financial circumstances.
